headline: Kawasaki Heavy Industries says it wants a fully autonomous humanoid robot on the market by 2030.
score_reason: Concrete target from a large industrial maker, but a plan rather than a working machine, and only the opening of the article was readable.
importance_line: Japan's heavy industry is joining the humanoid race with a home-grown AI platform, which matters to factory workers and to Japanese robot suppliers, though 2030 is far off and nothing has been demonstrated yet.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports that Kawasaki Heavy Industries plans to release a fully autonomous humanoid robot, powered by artificial intelligence, as soon as 2030. The machine is its Kaleido humanoid, under development since 2015, and it is to run on a so-called physical AI platform (software that lets a robot perceive and act in the real world) being built in Japan by a company named Noetra.
notes: Paywalled; entry rests on the readable headline, subhead and first paragraph only. machine_action false: a plan, not a demonstration.
